Rashi on Shabbat 66b:10:1.hebrew: מאי איריא בנים - לרב יהודה פריך: אי קישורין דמתני' לרפואת חולי נינהו, מאי איריא בנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:10:1.english: Why specifically boys - [The Gemara] raises an objection against Rav Yehuda: If the knots of the Mishnah are for healing an illness, why specifically boys?

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:11:1.hebrew: געגועין - ברמור"ט, מגעגע עליו ואינו יכול ליפרד ממנו. ורפואה זו לא שייכא בנקבות, שאין האב מחבבן כל כך מתחילתן שיהיו מגעגעין עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:11:1.english: Longings - [In Old French:] bramort [yearning] — he yearns for him and cannot part from him. And this remedy is not applicable to females, for the father does not cherish them so much from the beginning that they would yearn for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:11:2.hebrew: תפילין - שיד ימינו קושרתו לשמאלו, זהו סימן לגירסא:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:11:2.english: Phylacteries - For one's right hand ties it to one's left [arm]; this is a mnemonic for the textual reading:

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:12:1.hebrew: סחופי כסא - כוס שיש בו הבל, כגון שעירו ממנו מים חמין, וכופהו על הטיבור למי שחש במעיו. ואוחז הכוס את הבשר, ומושך אליו את המעיים, ומושיבן במקומן:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:12:1.english: Overturning a cup - A cup that contains vapor, such as when they poured hot water out of it, and [one] inverts it over the navel for someone who feels pain in his bowels. And the cup grips the flesh, pulls the intestines toward itself, and settles them in their place.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:13:1.english: To smear - On the palms of his hands and the soles of his feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:1.hebrew: דרב הונא מבי רב - שהיה בא מבי רב, שהוא רבו; וכן רב מבי ר' חייא, ור' חייא מבי רבי:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:1.english: Of Rav Huna from the house of Rav - That he was coming from the house of Rav, who was his teacher; and likewise Rav from the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya, and Rabbi Ḥiyya from the house of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:2.hebrew: מבסמי - שכורין. שהיו משקין את התלמידים, ואלו — מפני שחשובין הן — היו עושין להן דבר להפג את יינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:2.english: Drunk - Intoxicated. For they would give the disciples [wine] to drink, and for these [disciples], because they were distinguished, they would do something to dispel their wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:3.hebrew: לגוייתא דידייהו - תוכי ידיהם, דהיינו כף:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:3.english: The insides of their hands - The insides of their hands, that is, the palm.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:4.english: That becomes clear - For it progressively becomes clear at all times from the heat of the flesh.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:5.english: The sealing clay of a barrel - The stopper of the barrel.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:14:6.english: That this sealing [clay] loosens - On account of the water.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:15:1.hebrew: ליחנק - מי שנפרקה חוליא של מפרקת צוארו ונופלת בגרונו — תולין אותו בראשו שיהא צוארו נפשט, ודומה לחניקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:15:1.english: To be strangled - One whose vertebra of the nape of his neck was dislocated and slips into his throat — they suspend him by his head so that his neck will be stretched out, and it resembles strangulation.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:16:1.hebrew: לפופי - לכורכו בבגדים וקושרו בחגורה רחבה, ומתיישבין פרקי אבריו, שהן רכין ונשמטין בחבלי הלידה. וקורין אנמלטויי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:16:1.english: Swaddling - To wrap him in cloths and bind him with a wide sash, so that the joints of his limbs settle [into place], as they are soft and dislocated by the travails of childbirth. And they call [this] enmailloter [to swaddle] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:17:1.hebrew: מתני בנים - שתי שמועות דאיירי בקטנים, היה שונה בשם רבי (אבא) בר הונא משמיה דרב חמא בר גוריא:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:17:1.english: Taught "children" - He would teach two traditions that deal with minors in the name of Rabbi (Abba) bar Huna in the name of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:17:2.english: Child - One teaching that deals with a child is taught in his name:

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:17:3.english: Both of them - [The teachings regarding] longing and swaddling.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:18:1.hebrew: כל מנייני - כל לחישות. ומפני שכופלין אותן — יש ג' פעמים, ויש יותר — קרי להו מנייני:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:18:1.english: All counts - All incantations. And because they repeat them — some three times, and some more — [the Gemara] calls them "counts."

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:18:2.english: In the mother's name - [Such as:] So-and-so, son of so-and-so [female].

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:19:1.hebrew: דמיפרשי - כל לחשים שמפורש מניין, כמה פעמים שיאמרו ויכפלו אותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:19:1.english: That are specified - All incantations for which a count is specified, [as to] how many times they should recite and repeat it.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:19:2.hebrew: כדמפרשי - כופלין אותו כפי מניינו. ודלא מיפרשי בהם — סתם כפילתן ארבעין וחד זימנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:19:2.english: As they are specified - One repeats it according to its count. And [for those] in which [a count] is not specified — their standard repetition is forty-one times.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:1:1.hebrew: לתרוצי סוגיא - לתקן פסיעותיו ולזקוף קומה, מפני שרגליו ושוקיו רותתות, ולא לסמיכת כל גופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:1:1.english: To align his steps - To correct his steps and straighten [his] posture, because his feet and legs tremble, and not to support his entire body.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:1.hebrew: אבן תקומה - אבן שנושאות אותה נשים עוברות שלא יפילו, וקורין לה קוטאנ"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:1.english: A preservation stone - A stone that pregnant women carry so that they do not miscarry, and they call it contiene [supporter] in the vernacular.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:2.english: With the counterweight - Any object that was weighed against it.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:3.hebrew: ולא שהפילה - ולא תאמר שלא התירו לצאת בה אלא לאשה שעלולה להפיל עוברה, שהפילה כבר עובר אחר:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:3.english: And not that she miscarried - And do not say that they permitted going out with it only for a woman who is prone to miscarry her fetus, [in that] she already miscarried another fetus:

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:4.english: And not that she conceived - That it is known to her that she is pregnant.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:5.hebrew: והוא דאיכוין ותקל - שנמצא החפץ מאליו למשקל האבן, ולא שחיסרו ממנו או הוסיפו עליו לכוונו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:20:5.english: And this [is only] when it matched and was weighed - That the object was found on its own [to match] the weight of the stone, and not that they took away from it or added to it to adjust it.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:1.english: [A fever] of one day - That has seized him every day.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:2.english: A white zuz - [One that is] refined and new.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:3.hebrew: למלחתא - למקום שריפת המים, שעושין נגרים על שפת הים להמשיך מים לבריכות רחבות העשויות לכך. וכשנתמלאו, סותם החריצין, והשמש שורף את המים, שמלוחין הן, ונעשה מלח:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:3.english: To the salt pools - To the place of evaporating the water, where they make channels on the seashore to draw water into wide pools made for this [purpose]. And when they are filled, one blocks the trenches, and the sun evaporates the water, as it is salty, and it becomes salt.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:4.hebrew: בחללא דבי צוארו - תחת גרונו, כנגד מפתחי חלוקו. לשון רבינו הלוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:4.english: In the hollow of his neck - Beneath his throat, opposite the opening of his tunic. [This is] the wording of Rabbeinu HaLevi.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:21:5.english: A thread of hair - [The Old French word] lice [a heddle], made of hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:1.english: A crossroads - A place where two roads diverge.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:10.english: And let him say to it - To the ant.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:11.hebrew: טעונך עלי - מה שהיית נושא, אשאנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:11.english: Your burden is upon me - What you were carrying, I will carry.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:13.hebrew: איניש אשכחיה ואיפסיק ביה - חולי כזה שזה עושה. וכי אמר ליה ״טעונך עלי״ — זהו חולי של חברו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:13.english: A person found it and ended [his illness] with it - [Namely,] an illness such as this that this [person] is performing [a remedy for]. And when he says to it, “Your burden is upon me,” that [burden] is the illness of his fellow.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:2.english: A large ant - A large ant.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:3.english: That is carrying something - That is carrying anything.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:4.english: Let him take it - The ant.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:5.english: In a copper tube - A kind of copper tube:

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:6.english: And close it with lead - He should stop up its opening with lead.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:7.hebrew: גושפנקי - חותמות. ולאו דוקא שיתין נקט, ולאו דוקא חותמות של צורה, אלא סתימות הרבה זו על זו: שעוה על העופרת, ושוב זפת, ושוב טיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:7.english: Seals - Seals. And it did not mention "sixty" precisely, nor [did it mean] specifically seals with an engraved design, but rather many layers of sealing, one upon the other: wax over the lead, and then pitch, and then clay.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:8.english: And shake it - He should shake it.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:22:9.english: And lift it - He should carry it.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:23:1.english: A new jug - A small, new earthenware vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:23:3.hebrew: וליהדריה ז' זימני ארישיה - יקיפנו סביבות ראשו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:23:3.english: And let him turn it seven times around his head - He shall circle it around his head.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:4:1.english: I teach: A woman may perform ḥalitza with them - Evidently, it is called a shoe.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:1.hebrew: חמרא דאכפא - חמור הנישא בכתפיים — הליצנים עושין אותו, ונראה כמי שרוכב עליו, ובמקומנו נקרא ארדפיס"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:1.english: A donkey of the shoulders - A donkey carried on the shoulders — jesters make it, and [the person] appears like one who is riding upon it, and in our region it is called ardeficie [a hobbyhorse costume].

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:2.hebrew: קישורי - אשקצ"ש, שמהלכין בהם במקום טיט. וקשיא לי: נהי דטהורין מטומאת מגע, דפשוטי כלי עץ נינהו — אבל מן המדרס למה טהורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:2.english: Stilts - Eschaces [stilts in Old French], which they walk on in muddy places. And it is difficult to me: Granted that they are pure from contact impurity, as they are flat wooden articles; but from midras [treading] impurity, why are they pure?

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:3.hebrew: פרמי - טלמוסא הנקשרת על הפרצוף, להבעית הבנים קטנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:5:3.english: Peramei - A mask [talemasche] that is tied over the face to frighten young children.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:6:1.english: With knots - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:6:2.english: With bells - *Escheletes* [bells] of gold, for ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:7:1.english: Adda Mari - That is his name.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:7:2.hebrew: קשרי פואה - גרנצ"א. קושרים בקשרים ותולין בצואר לרפואה, ולא ידעתי לאיזה חולי:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:7:2.english: Knots of madder - Garance [madder]. They tie [it] in knots and hang [it] around the neck as a remedy, but I do not know for which illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:8:1.english: Maintain - They stabilize the illness so that it does not worsen.

Rashi on Shabbat 66b:9:2.hebrew: נפל פותא בבירא - נפל רפואת הפואה בבור, דאין אדם נזהר בכל אלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 66b:9:2.english: The madder fell into a pit - The remedy of the madder fell into a pit, for a person is not careful with all of these.

Tosafot on Shabbat 66b:7:1.hebrew: קישורי - פי' הקונטרס: אשקצ"ש. והקשה בקונטרס, ור"י תירץ: דכיון שאינם עשויים אלא ללכת דרך העברה בטיט — אינו טמא מדרס. ובערוך פירש: דקישורי היינו אשקצ"ש שעושין הליצני, והן גבוהין מאד, ואינן אלא לרקד עליהן, ולא להילוך עבידי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 66b:7:1.english: Kishurei - The Kuntres explained: eschaces [stilts]. And [Rashi] raised a difficulty in the Kuntres, and the Ri resolved [it]: Since they are made only to walk by way of passing through mud, [such an implement] is not susceptible to midras impurity. And in the Arukh, he explained that kishurei are eschaces [stilts] that entertainers make, and they are very tall, and they are [used] only to dance upon them, and are not made for walking.
